old_proper.name: Hymn at the Translation of the Blessed Sacrament
old_proper.notes: Printed locus printed p. 160, DE SOLEMNI TRANSLATIONE AC REPOSITIONE SACRAMENTI, rubric n. 3; artifact PDF p. 241. No marginal number: the cue stands inside a rubric, not as a numbered text.. Preexisting material under 17 U.S.C. 103(b), corroborated in the tracked public-domain Pustet Ratisbon 1862 at printed p. 162 (Feria V. in Coena Domini, rubric for the procession to the repository); text-layer lines 31630-31633. The hymn is sung as far as Tantum ergo during the procession, and repeated if need be; Tantum ergo is sung at the place of reposition.
old_proper.text:
Dum fit processio, cantatur hymnus Pange, lingua, gloriosi Corporis
mysterium, usque ad verba Tantum ergo; si vero opus sit, idem hymnus
repetitur.

old_latin_provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 adds the extent (`usque ad verba Tantum ergo`) and the repetition clause; 1862 gives the cue bare. That is rubric, not hymn text.; 1962 points the incipit `Pange, lingua, gloriosi Corporis mysterium`; 1862 sets it unpointed. Corroboration: none attempted.
old_latin_provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
old_latin_provenance.publication_locator: Pustet Ratisbon 1862, printed p. 162 (Feria V. in Coena Domini, rubric for the procession to the repository); text-layer lines 31630-31633; artifact rights_status public-domain on a book first published in 1862
old_latin_provenance.publication_evidence: The wording is preexisting material of the 1962 typical edition under 17 U.S.C. 103(b), which gives a revised edition no exclusive right in material it did not contribute. The independent registered public-domain witness is the tracked 1862 Pustet text artifact. The position is settled for the repository at src/sources/inventories/missale-romanum-1962-facsimile-rights-v1.toml, which names the seasonal orations as preexisting material and requires exactly this pairing of 103(b) with a public-domain witness.
